name: architect
sentence: Sketch types, signatures, and module structure before code, then stay in the loop while implementation fills in.

name: arena
sentence: Spawn N parallel candidates at the same task, pick a base, graft the strongest parts of the losers into it.

name: Authoring or modifying a skill
sentence: **You own the skill's voice.** 1.

name: automate-me
sentence: Use for "automate me", "create/update/refresh my -mode skill", "turn/capture my preferences or working style into a skill", or wanting agents to follow how the user works.

name: Autonomous run
sentence: **You own the exit condition.

name: Autopilot-full
sentence: **You own the verdicts, never the PRs.

name: Autopilot-stack
sentence: Run the Autopilot-full playbook, but do not merge.

name: Babysit
sentence: **You own the merge frontier.

name: benchmark-checklist
sentence: Vet a perf measurement (limiter, tuning, limits, errors, repeatability, relevance, and whether the work happened) before you report or act on it.

name: blast-radius
sentence: Find what a change could break somewhere else before it ships, beyond the diff, and prove the one fact it's safe because of by running real code instead of writing it up.

name: bro
sentence: Restate the last message in plain human language, with no jargon.

name: Bug fix
sentence: **You own this task.

name: correct
sentence: Find the mistakes agents keep repeating in this repo and make each one impossible.

name: create-formal-verification-skill
sentence: Generate a project-local skill that formally verifies the code where a bug costs the most and tests reach the least, in any language, with whichever verification tool fits.

name: create-verification-skill
sentence: Generate a project-local verification skill that drives your app the way a user does — any language, framework, or platform.

name: Eval
sentence: **You own the experiment design.

name: Feature
sentence: **You own the design.

name: figure-it-out
sentence: Design an auditable playbook when no narrower one fits: a large migration, an ambitious multi-part change, or work a human reviews after stepping away.

name: Hillclimb
sentence: **You own the metric and the experiment's integrity.

name: how
sentence: Use for "how does X work", code walkthroughs before changing something, and placement / ownership / layering questions ("where should this live", "which package owns this", "is this the right layer").

name: in-your-own-words
sentence: Restate in your own words what you think the user's goals are and what problem they're trying to solve.

name: interrogate
sentence: Use for "interrogate", "adversarial review", "multi-model review", "challenge this", "stress test this code", "find blind spots", or "tear this apart".

name: Investigation
sentence: **You own the answer.

name: ketchup
sentence: Catch the user up on what changed in this chat since their last message, in plain words and small visuals.

name: ketchup-video
sentence: Catch the user up like /ketchup, with a short subtitled video of slides for what happened and the waiting calls as text under it.

name: maintain-formal-verification-skill
sentence: Bring a project's formal verification back in line with the code after the code changes: find the commits that touched verified code, update the model, harness, or properties to describe the code as it is now, rerun, and say whether each failure is drift in the verification or a bug in the code.

name: maintain-verification-skill
sentence: Periodic pass that keeps a project's verification skill and feature map honest: parallel source readers per feature, one live session driving every feature, at most one PR of proven corrections.

name: make-bot-ui
sentence: Use when building a custom UI (page, dashboard, buttons) that should wake a Grok Bot over a webhook, when the user must provide a webhook sender key, or when exposing that UI on Tailscale.

name: Multi-phase or multi-PR plan
sentence: **You own the plan, not the code.

name: no-comments
sentence: Spawn Comment Sicko, fix accepted findings, and offer encodings for claimed constraints.

name: Opening a PR
sentence: Invoked at the end of every other playbook.

name: Pause safely
sentence: **You own a clean stop.

name: Perf issue
sentence: **You own the measurement story.

name: poteto-help
sentence: Guides users through pstack setup, /poteto-mode, and picking the skill, playbook, or principle for a task.

name: poteto-mode
sentence: poteto's agent style for concise, detailed responses, deliberate subagents, unslopped prose, simple code, and verified work.

name: principle-attack-the-premise
sentence: Apply when two or more fixes that share one premise have failed the same gate.

name: principle-boundary-discipline
sentence: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters.

name: principle-build-the-lever
sentence: Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks.

name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
sentence: Apply when you catch yourself writing the same instruction a second time, or notice a recurring correction.

name: principle-exhaust-the-design-space
sentence: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase.

name: principle-experience-first
sentence: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up.

name: principle-explain-the-number
sentence: Apply before you measure, and before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result.

name: principle-fix-root-causes
sentence: Apply when debugging.

name: principle-foundational-thinking
sentence: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share.

name: principle-guard-the-context-window
sentence: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning.

name: principle-laziness-protocol
sentence: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading.

name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
sentence: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries.

name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
sentence: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist.

name: principle-minimize-reader-load
sentence: Apply when reviewing or shaping code that's hard to trace.

name: principle-model-the-domain
sentence: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files.

name: principle-never-block-on-the-human
sentence: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work.

name: principle-outcome-oriented-execution
sentence: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries.

name: principle-prove-it-works
sentence: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done.

name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
sentence: Apply when integrating a new requirement into an existing design.

name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
sentence: Apply when concurrent actors might write to the same file, branch, key, or state object.

name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
sentence: Apply to multi-step work (sweeps, migrations, runs of similar edits) and to how you stack commits and PRs.

name: principle-subtract-before-you-add
sentence: Apply when sequencing an addition, refactor, or rewrite.

name: principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
sentence: Apply when you write, change, or keep a test.

name: principle-type-system-discipline
sentence: Apply when designing types, reviewing a function signature, or writing code in any statically-typed language.

name: Prototype
sentence: **You own the design decision, not the code.

name: recall
sentence: Reconstruct your recent working context from your own chat history, live state, and the shared record (user reports, prior fixes, incidents), then hand back a tight current-state brief.

name: Refactoring
sentence: **You own the contract.

name: reflect
sentence: Mine the active transcript for durable learnings and route each to a concrete edit on an existing skill.

name: reframe
sentence: Teach the expert words for what the operator is building, borrow words from neighboring fields that solved the same problem, then rewrite their description with them.

name: reproduce-and-fix-issues
sentence: Reproduce triaged Slack bugs through a configured app-control adapter, verify existing fixes, and open a bounded draft pull request only after before-and-after proof.

name: Runtime forensics
sentence: **You own the diagnosis.

name: Session pickup
sentence: **You own the resume point.

name: setup-benny
sentence: Configure Benny and prepare its triage and repro automations.

name: setup-pstack
sentence: Configure which models pstack uses per role and at what reasoning budget.

name: sharpen
sentence: Make a task deeper, not bigger, then rewrite the prompt.

name: Shipping
sentence: **You own what lands.

name: show-me-your-work
sentence: Keep a reviewable decision trail for long-running or unattended work: a TSV log with one row per decision (what, why, evidence, result).

name: statechart
sentence: Check a TLA+ model of a system that moves between states, such as a product flow, a protocol, or a service, and draw it as a Mermaid statechart.

name: swarm
sentence: Fan out N parallel workers, drain them, and return one report.

name: tdd
sentence: Use only when the user explicitly asks for TDD, a failing test, or a regression test, OR when the bug has an obvious cheap local test target.

name: teach
sentence: Explain a body of work plainly so a person actually understands it.

name: technical-writing
sentence: Layered technical-writing standard: Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax.

name: Trace forensics
sentence: **You own the diagnosis from the artifact.** Distinct from **Runtime forensics**, which instruments the live process.

name: triage-issue-reports
sentence: Triage Slack issue reports with one thread-only verdict, evidence review, cause-aware routing, tracker dedupe, and fail-closed ticket creation.

name: typescript-best-practices
sentence: TypeScript best practices.

name: unslop
sentence: Cut AI tells from any writing.

name: Visual parity
sentence: **You own pixel-exact equivalence.

name: why
sentence: Use for 'why does X work this way', 'why we picked Y', design rationale, regressions, postmortems, or data-backed thresholds.

name: ub-mode
sentence: Follow the reduced principles when writing or changing code.
